$comment: Generated by orchestrator/backend/scripts/generate_agent_schemas.py from app.api.assessment.FindingRecordRequest plus agent-side overlays where the CLI contract is intentionally stricter than the backend model.

slug.title: Slug
slug.description: Stable kebab-case identifier for this finding (e.g. 'sqli-search-q'). Omit to auto-generate.

title.title: Title
title.description: One-line finding name: vuln class + location (e.g. 'Blind SQL injection in /search?q').

severity.title: Severity
severity.description: CVSS-aligned impact rating. Use 'critical' only for CVSS >=9.0 or trivially exploitable RCE/auth-bypass.

workflow_status.title: Workflow Status
workflow_status.description: Lifecycle state settable at record time. New findings: 'active'. Post-exploitation confirmed: 'exploited'. WAF/control stopped testing: 'blocked'. Duplicate absorbed into another record: 'merged'. Delivered to client: 'reported'. NOTE: the blue-team/IR states (contained, eradicated, recovered) are intentionally NOT recordable here — they are applied only via `vigil assess update-finding`, so this record-finding enum is deliberately narrower than the full WorkflowStatus vocabulary.

verification_state.title: Verification State
verification_state.description: Human review state. Leave 'unreviewed' when first recording; set 'verified' after confirming exploitability; 'disputed' when contested.

verification_disposition.title: Verification Disposition
verification_disposition.description: Verifier outcome (stored field). 'none': not yet checked. 'pending_runtime_proof': needs live PoC. 'blocked': the attempt could not even start (missing provisioning); requires details.block_reason and is held OUT of the report. 'confirmed': exploitability proven. 'downgraded': real but severity reduced. 'false_positive': not exploitable. NOTE: `vigil assess verify-finding --disposition` additionally accepts 'disputed', which is a verify ACTION that sets verification_state='disputed' and leaves this field at 'none' — 'disputed' is never persisted as a disposition, so it is intentionally absent from this stored enum.

defect_family.title: Defect Family
defect_family.description: Short vuln-class label for grouping (e.g. 'sql-injection', 'buffer-overflow', 'ssrf'). Use kebab-case.

root_cause_key.title: Root Cause Key
root_cause_key.description: Stable key linking variants to a shared root cause (e.g. 'missing-input-sanitization-search'). Omit if not part of a variant cluster.

auth_context.title: Auth Context
auth_context.description: Authentication state when the finding was triggered. Use 'anonymous', a role name (e.g. 'user', 'admin'), or credential slug.

canonical_location.title: Canonical Location
canonical_location.description: Primary affected location. URL for network findings (e.g. 'https://target.example/search?q'); 'file:path:line' for code findings.

summary.title: Summary
summary.description: 2-5 sentence description: what is vulnerable, how it is triggered, and the attacker impact.

evidence_ref.title: Evidence Ref
evidence_ref.description: Path or identifier for supporting artifact (e.g. 'scans/sqlmap.txt', 'artifacts/burp-export.xml'). Leave empty if evidence is inline in details.evidence.

notes.title: Notes
notes.description: Freeform operational notes: retesting observations, partial progress, raw tool output. Not shown in reports.

source_name.title: Source Name
source_name.description: Agent or tool that produced this record (e.g. 'vulnerability-analyst', 'nuclei'). Mirrors provenance.agent_name for quick filtering.

discovered_by.description: Agent name that first identified this finding (e.g. 'vulnerability-analyst').

owasp_category.description: OWASP Top 10 2021 category code and name (e.g. 'A03:2021 Injection').

cwe_id.description: CWE identifier (e.g. 'CWE-89' for SQL injection, 'CWE-122' for heap buffer overflow).

parameter.description: Exact name of the affected input: query param, header, JSON key, or form field (e.g. 'q', 'X-User-Id', 'username').

slot_type.description: Code-analysis input class for the attack (e.g. 'URL-COMPONENT', 'NETWORK-INPUT', 'PROTOCOL-FIELD').

request_method.description: HTTP verb that triggers the finding (e.g. 'GET', 'POST', 'PUT', 'DELETE').

evidence.description: Verbatim proof: exact response excerpt, artifact path, or replayable request/response. Must be sufficient to reproduce independently.

kill_reason.description: Verifier rationale for false_positive verdict: which check failed and why the issue is not exploitable.

kill_check.description: Verification check number (1-5) that produced the false-positive verdict.

entry_point.description: Where attacker-controlled data enters the program (e.g. 'curl_url_set(CURLURLPART_URL, attacker_url)', 'POST /upload body field filename').

sink.description: Dangerous operation that consumes tainted data (e.g. 'memcpy(buf, scheme, schemelen) at lib/urlapi.c:342', 'sqlite3_exec(db, query)').

taint_path.description: Arrow-delimited data flow from entry_point to sink (e.g. 'curl_url_set -> parseurl() -> memcpy(buf, scheme, schemelen)').

guards_evaluated.description: List each relevant bounds/validation check and state whether it is absent, bypassable, or ineffective (e.g. 'No bounds check on schemelen before memcpy').

impact.description: Concrete attacker outcome: what data is exposed or what action can be taken, and who is affected (e.g. 'Anonymous attacker can read all DB rows', 'Remote code execution via heap corruption').

cvss_score.description: CVSS 3.1 base score (0.1-10.0). Must match cvss_vector.

remediation.description: Specific fix or missing control (e.g. 'Use parameterized queries', 'Add bounds check on schemelen before memcpy').

steps_to_reproduce.description: Ordered reproduction steps, one action per string. Start from initial access state; end at impact observation.

poc_code.description: Minimal exploit code or script that reproduces the finding. Omit if poc_request/poc_response is sufficient.

poc_request.description: HTTP request that triggers the vulnerability.

poc_response.description: Observed HTTP response that confirms the vulnerability.

references.description: CVE IDs, NVD/advisory URLs, or CWE links relevant to this finding.

chain_required.description: Set true only when this finding has no standalone impact and is meaningful only as part of an exploit chain.

chain_rationale.description: Required when chain_required is true: explain which chain step this enables and why standalone impact is insufficient.

required_followup.description: Concrete next steps needed to validate or complete the chain (e.g. 'Confirm reachable network caller for the URL parser').

roe_blocked.description: Set true when the primitive is proved but the program's rules of engagement forbid the final proof step; grade at impact-if-true. Distinct from a provisioning/access wall (see block_reason) and from chain_required (which needs another bug).

block_reason.description: Why the finding cannot be advanced right now — a provisioning/access wall blocking the next proof step (as opposed to an ROE policy wall or a missing-bug chain park). Surfaced in the resume-brief Attempts ledger.

unblock_requirements.description: What must be provisioned to lift the block so the finding can be driven to proof. When the unblocker is another finding or chain, link it with `vigil assess link-finding <slug> --link-kind unblocked_by ...`.

kind.description: Category of what is needed: account | line | device | credential | access.

description.description: Concretely what to provision (e.g. 'a test account in the org-admin group with role-management entitlement').

requested_from.description: Who can provide it (e.g. 'program contact', 'target admin').

attempts_summary.description: One-line summary of what was tried and the result, for the resume-brief Attempts ledger (e.g. 'anonymous + member + billing-admin sessions all 403 at the function gate').

variant_of.description: Slug of the root finding when this record is a verified same-class variant (e.g. 'sqli-search-q').

original_pattern.description: Abstract pattern signature copied verbatim from the root finding during variant analysis.

agent_name.description: Agent that produced this finding (e.g. 'vulnerability-analyst'). Mirror of source_name.

artifact.description: Path or ID of the artifact this finding was derived from.

evidence_type.title: Evidence Type
evidence_type.description: Strength of evidence. 'network-confirmed': live exploit or observed response. 'code-inferred': static/dataflow analysis without runtime proof. 'theoretical': logic-based hypothesis, no code or traffic evidence. 'informational': non-exploitable observation.

submission_status.title: Submission Status
submission_status.description: External bug-bounty/program submission state, ORTHOGONAL to workflow_status (report-inclusion). 'none': not submitted. 'submitted': sent to the program. 'accepted'/'rejected'/'duplicate': program triage outcome. 'needs_info': program requested more detail. Omit to keep the default 'none'.

request_variant_id.title: Request Variant Id
request_variant_id.description: ID of the request variant this finding concerns. Recorded as a finding_link to that request-variant surface, not stored as a finding column. Omit when the finding is not tied to a specific request variant.

service_id.title: Service Id
service_id.description: ID of the service this finding concerns. Recorded as a finding_link to that service surface, not stored as a finding column. Omit when the finding is not tied to a specific service.

surface_id.title: Surface Id
surface_id.description: ID of the attack surface this finding concerns. Recorded as a finding_link to that surface, not stored as a finding column. Omit when the finding is not tied to a specific surface.

target_kind.title: Target Kind
target_kind.description: Entity type of the link target (e.g. 'finding', 'credential', 'access_record', 'attack_chain').

target_id.title: Target Id
target_id.description: Database ID of the target entity. Provide target_id OR target_ref, not both.

target_ref.title: Target Ref
target_ref.description: Slug or string reference for the target when target_id is unavailable.

notes.title: Notes
notes.description: Why this link exists or how the two entities are related.

title: Assessment Finding Record

examples.title: Blind SQL injection in search
examples.summary: Boolean-blind SQL injection on the search endpoint

details.impact: Anonymous attackers can extract arbitrary data from the backing store
details.remediation: Use parameterized queries for all search input

examples.title: Heap buffer overflow in URL parser via overlong scheme
examples.summary: Attacker-controlled URL scheme exceeding 64 bytes overflows heap buffer in parseurl()

details.impact: Remote code execution via heap corruption
details.evidence: memcpy(buf, scheme, schemelen) copies attacker-controlled bytes without a bounds check
details.taint_path: curl_url_set(CURLURLPART_URL, attacker_url) -> parseurl() -> memcpy(buf, scheme, schemelen)
details.guards_evaluated: No bounds check on schemelen before memcpy
details.remediation: Add bounds check on schemelen before memcpy; reject URLs with scheme longer than 63 bytes
details.chain_rationale: The primitive is meaningful for exploitation, but final report impact depends on chaining it to a reachable crash or controlled allocation path.
required_followup: Exercise the URL parser through a network-reachable caller
Confirm whether the overflow produces controlled corruption under sanitizer instrumentation

examples.title: BFLA on role-grant endpoint (blocked: needs org-admin group)
examples.summary: The role-grant endpoint appears to lack function-level authz, but confirming it requires an account provisioned into the org-admin group.
examples.notes: Anonymous + member roles 403 at the gate; the grant call is only reachable once inside org-admin — provisioning not available this engagement.

details.impact: If confirmed, a low-privilege user could grant themselves arbitrary roles (privilege escalation).
details.evidence: GET /api/roles/grant returns 403 for member; the UI only renders the grant control for org-admin.
details.block_reason: Cannot reach the role-grant endpoint without an org-admin-group account.

unblock_requirements.description: A test account provisioned into the org-admin group with role-management entitlement.

details.attempts_summary: Tried anonymous, member, and billing-admin sessions; all 403 at the function gate. Recorded via block-technique (BFLA on this host).
